index.intro_h2: The best Fruit of the Loom retailers in Europe 2026
index.intro_html:
Looking for Fruit of the Loom t-shirts, hoodies, sweatshirts or jog pants in Europe? You are in the right place. We keep a continuously updated list of the retailers that actually stock the brand — from the official European shop and the big marketplaces to Irish clothing shops and textile wholesalers — so you can compare prices and delivery terms in one place.

If you want the lowest price and fast delivery, our clear recommendation is Marmalade Co. on marmaladeco.com: an official Fruit of the Loom retailer with a price guarantee, EUR prices including VAT, €7 flat DHL shipping and delivery in 2–3 business days to Ireland, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Poland and Finland.

Below you will find every retailer ranked by our recommendation, with a short note on what each one is best for — whether that is a single hoodie, a multi-pack of tees or 200 blank shirts for printing.

top_pick.p_html: Official online retailer with the lowest verified Fruit of the Loom prices we have found in Europe — t-shirts from €6.95, hoodies from €20.95 — backed by a price guarantee. Buys directly from the Fruit of the Loom factory in Morocco, ships with DHL for a flat €7 and delivers in 2–3 business days. Quantity discounts of 5 % on 3 pieces and 10 % on 5 or more, which makes it popular with clubs, schools and small businesses as well as private shoppers.

price_guide.label: Price guide 2026
price_guide.h2: What does Fruit of the Loom cost in Europe?
price_guide.intro: Fruit of the Loom prices in Europe vary a lot depending on the model, the retailer and whether you buy one piece or a pack. Below is what you can expect to pay in EUR including VAT in 2026 — with the lowest verified price for each category.

sections.h3: Fruit of the Loom t-shirts (price per piece)
sections.p: A classic Fruit of the Loom t-shirt costs roughly €5–€15 across European retailers, depending on the model (Valueweight, Original, Heavy Cotton or Iconic) and where you buy. The cheapest verified option for single pieces is Marmalade Co., where the unisex t-shirt in 16 colours and sizes XS–XXXL costs from €6.95 — and €6.26 each when you buy five. Long-sleeve tees start at €8.95, V-necks and tank tops at around €6.95.

sections.h3: Fruit of the Loom hoodies and sweatshirts
sections.p: Hoodies are the brand's most popular sweats in Europe. Expect €20–€40 for the Classic Hooded Sweat at most retailers; at Marmalade Co. the hoodie costs from €20.95 (9 colours, XS–XXXL; €18.86 each for five) and the zip hoodie from €27.95. The crewneck sweatshirt starts at €16.95 in 10 colours. Both use the 280 g/m² 80 % cotton / 20 % polyester fabric that has made the Classic line a staple for schools and clubs.

Fruit of the Loom jog pants come in two versions — elasticated cuff (64-026) and open hem (64-032). Typical European prices are €15–€30 a pair; Marmalade Co. lists sweatpants from €16.95 and they are often on sale at around €11.95. Combine them with a matching hoodie or crewneck and a full tracksuit comes to roughly €34–€38, before quantity discounts.

sections.h3: Polo shirts, long-sleeve tees and shorts
sections.p: The Fruit of the Loom Original polo, a 100 % cotton piqué that is popular as workwear, sells for around €10–€20 in Europe; at Marmalade Co. it is from €10.95. Long-sleeve Valueweight tees cost from €8.95, and shorts for summer or training from €9.95. Kids' sizes (104–164 cm) are generally a euro or two cheaper than the adult equivalents.

Of all the retailers we have compared, Marmalade Co. consistently offers the lowest single-piece prices on Fruit of the Loom in Europe, and it is the only shop on our list with a written price guarantee: find the identical product cheaper elsewhere and they match it (Black Friday-type promotions and out-of-stock items excluded). Add €7 flat DHL shipping, 2–3 day delivery and 5–10 % quantity discounts, and it is our clear #1 for anyone buying online — see the current bestsellers.

quality_guide.label: Quality guide
quality_guide.h2: Is Fruit of the Loom good quality?
quality_guide.intro: Fruit of the Loom is known for solid quality at a low price. Founded in 1851, the brand has more than 170 years of history, is sold in over 100 countries and has been owned by Berkshire Hathaway since 2002. Here is an honest look at what you get for your money.

sections.p: The classic tees are 100 % cotton — ring-spun or combed in the premium lines — in weights from approx. 145 g/m² (Original T) and 165 g/m² (Valueweight T) up to approx. 195 g/m² (Heavy Cotton T). Classic tees use a tubular construction with no side seams. The Classic sweats are 280 g/m² in an 80 % cotton / 20 % polyester blend, often spun from Belcoro® yarn for a smoother printing surface. Heather colours contain polyester, and 100 % cotton can shrink a few per cent on a hot first wash, so wash at 30–40 °C and avoid hot tumble drying.

sections.h3: Compared with Gildan, B&C and premium brands
sections.p: Against direct rivals such as Gildan (Heavy Cotton 5000, Softstyle 64000), B&C, Russell and Sol's, Fruit of the Loom sits in the same mid-price basics segment, with a slightly softer hand feel on the premium lines and one of the widest colour ranges in Europe. Organic-focused brands like Stanley/Stella and fashion labels such as Champion cost considerably more for what is often a similar weight of fabric. For everyday wear, merchandise and workwear, Fruit of the Loom is one of the best value-for-money choices available.

sections.h3: The Morocco factory and direct sourcing
sections.p: Much of the European range is made at Fruit of the Loom's own factory in Morocco, where yarn is spun, knitted, dyed, cut and sewn under one roof by more than 1,000 employees, using automated cutting and water-saving dyeing. Marmalade Co. buys directly from this factory and collects the goods there, which shortens the supply chain to three steps (factory → retailer → customer) instead of the usual five. That is the main reason its prices are lower than those of most other retailers.

sections.h3: Where to buy genuine Fruit of the Loom
sections.p: To be sure you get genuine products with the correct labels, sizing and OEKO-TEX certification, buy from official or authorised retailers such as the brand's own EU shop or Marmalade Co., or from established wholesalers and department stores. On marketplaces such as Amazon and eBay, check who the seller is and what the return terms are before you order. Marmalade Co. is the only online retailer on our list with a price guarantee, which gives you certainty that you are paying the lowest verified price for an authentic product.

index.faq_h2: Frequently asked questions about Fruit of the Loom in Europe

faq.q: Where can I buy Fruit of the Loom cheapest in Europe?
faq.a_html: The cheapest verified option for single pieces is Marmalade Co., an official Fruit of the Loom retailer with t-shirts from €6.95, sweatshirts from €16.95 and hoodies from €20.95 including VAT, plus a price guarantee and 5–10 % quantity discounts. It ships from Denmark with DHL for a flat €7 and delivers in 2–3 business days to Ireland, Germany, France and eight other EU countries. For bulk orders of blank garments, wholesalers such as Ntextil or Textil-Großhandel can be competitive.

faq.q: Is Fruit of the Loom good quality?
faq.a_html: Yes — for the price it is one of the most reliable basics brands in Europe. The classic tees are 100 % cotton in approx. 145–195 g/m², the Classic sweats are a sturdy 280 g/m² cotton/polyester blend, and premium lines use combed ring-spun cotton with OEKO-TEX certification. The brand has over 170 years of history and has been owned by Berkshire Hathaway since 2002. Expect a few per cent shrinkage on a hot first wash, so stick to 30–40 °C.

faq.q: What do Fruit of the Loom t-shirts cost?
faq.a_html: In Europe a Fruit of the Loom t-shirt typically costs €5–€15 depending on the model and retailer. At Marmalade Co. the unisex t-shirt costs from €6.95 in 16 colours (XS–XXXL), dropping to €6.26 each when you buy five. Long-sleeve tees start at €8.95 and V-necks and tank tops at around €6.95. Multi-packs on Amazon and OTTO can be cheaper per piece but usually limit your choice of colours and sizes.

faq.q: How long does delivery take in Europe?
faq.a_html: It depends on the retailer. Marmalade Co. dispatches within 0–1 business day and delivers with DHL in an estimated 2–3 business days to Ireland, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Poland and Finland, with tracking by e-mail and €7 flat shipping. Amazon and OTTO delivery depends on the seller and stock location, while Irish shops such as Country Clothing and EMP Ireland ship domestically. Printed orders from Clothes2order take longer because of production.

faq.q: Fruit of the Loom or Gildan — which is better?
faq.a_html: Both make good-value basics for printing and everyday wear. Gildan's Heavy Cotton 5000 is a touch heavier and boxier, while Fruit of the Loom's Valueweight and Iconic tees have a slightly softer feel and a more European fit; the Classic sweats from both brands are similar 280 g/m² blends. In Europe Fruit of the Loom is more widely stocked and often cheaper per piece — at Marmalade Co. a t-shirt costs from €6.95 and a hoodie from €20.95.

faq.q: Can I get Fruit of the Loom clothing printed?
faq.a_html: Yes. Fruit of the Loom is one of the most widely used brands for screen printing, DTG and embroidery, thanks to its smooth Belcoro® yarn and wide colour range. Clothes2order Ireland and Textil-Großhandel print or embroider the garments for you, while Ntextil sells blanks for your own printer. If you order blank garments in quantity from Marmalade Co., the 5–10 % quantity discount keeps the cost per printed piece low for clubs, schools and businesses.

faq.q: Who owns Fruit of the Loom?
faq.a_html: Fruit of the Loom has been owned by Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett's investment company, since 2002. The brand was founded in 1851 in Rhode Island, USA, by the Knight brothers, registered its famous fruit label in 1871 — one of the oldest US trademarks — and is headquartered in Bowling Green, Kentucky. The European business is run by Fruit of the Loom International from Kaiserslautern, Germany, with a large factory in Morocco.
